meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Colloquial. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to infuriate, to annoy', paired with 'взбесить'.

examples.trans: This noise is driving me crazy.
Why does everything around here bother me?

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening
E.g. a school evening. Common masculine noun meaning 'evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.
Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: For emphasis.

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: Core Russian part meaning 'even' in everyday speech.
на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.trans: Don't forget to wash the toilet.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

meanings.note: Auditory sensation or TV volume. Common masculine noun meaning 'sound, volume' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Turn up the volume on the television, please.

examples.text: Не дышать, я хочу слышать каждый тихий звук.
examples.trans: Do not breathe, I want to hear every quiet sound.

meanings.note: играть в + accusative (a game/sport)

examples.text: Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.
The children are playing in the courtyard.

examples.text: Хорошая фотография! Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Good photo! Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
+ infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Bring to memory. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'помнить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remind', paired with 'напоминать'.

examples.trans: Lyosha, remind us, what is this?
He reminded his friend about the meeting.

examples.text: Да, я лично напомнила шефу об этом.
examples.trans: Yes, I personally reminded the chef about this.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
With не / нет. Core Russian det meaning 'no ... at all, not any' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I have no money at all.

examples.text: Да нет у тебя никаких денег.
examples.trans: But you don't have any money.

отключить.gloss: to switch off, to cut off

meanings.note: Отключить свет = cut the power. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to switch off, to cut off', paired with 'отключать'.
Отключить свет = cut the power. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to switch off, to cut off', paired with 'отключать'.

examples.text: И позвони Цыганкову, пусть отключат свет.
examples.trans: And phone Tsygankov, have them cut the power.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'plan' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The mayor came up with a new plan.

examples.text: Но мэр придумал новый план. Сосед мэра теперь пойдёт в мэры.
examples.trans: But the mayor came up with a new plan. The mayor's neighbour will now run for mayor.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'везти'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'give a ride'.

examples.text: Я решил заехать за коллегой и подвезти на работу.
examples.trans: I decided to pick up my colleague and give her a ride to work.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и подвезти вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and give a ride on time.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: To keep in memory. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to remember'.

examples.trans: Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.note: takes the accusative; everyday synonym of о

examples.trans: He says nasty things about me.

examples.text: Как интересно! А в Москве ты про меня гадости рассказываешь.
examples.trans: How interesting! And in Moscow you go around saying nasty things about me.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'man', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: Louis, get away from me, you naughty man!
Make revenue for that obnoxious German?

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common feminine noun meaning 'Friday' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В пятницу у Лёвы день рождения.
examples.trans: On Friday it is Lyova's birthday.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть пятница.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always Friday.

meanings.note: День рождения = birthday. Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'birth' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Смотрите, врунишка новую машину купил! У врунишки сегодня день рождения!
examples.trans: Look, the little liar bought a new car! It's the little liar's birthday today!

meanings.note: The г sounds like в.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: + accusative. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.
the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'
'Слушаю' = I'm listening. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'Wednesday', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('environment, medium') (surrounding environment) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell me, is today really Wednesday?

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

увидеться.gloss: to see each other, meet up

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see each other, meet up', paired with 'видеться'.

examples.text: Послушай, мы сегодня увидимся вечером с тобой?
examples.trans: Listen, will we see each other this evening?
All right, see you in the kitchen, administrator!

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.
